blocks.title: Two ways to make a visual explanation

columns.label: Free-form HTML
columns.body_md:
A flexible canvas for a bespoke illustration.

- Every document carries layout decisions.
- Content and styling can become tangled.
- Review includes executable markup.

columns.label: Structured blocks
columns.body_md:
A shared visual language for recurring explanatory work.

- The author chooses the form of the idea.
- The renderer owns consistent presentation.
- Validation catches structural mistakes early.

blocks.title: Support the conclusion
blocks.summary: Distinguish inspected facts, illustrative readings, and questions that still need an answer.

blocks.text_md: The renderer imports the bundled schema validator before generating HTML. Its output embeds CSS and contains no browser script. Those are implementation properties, not claims about the source material being explained.

blocks.body_md: The evidence above describes the renderer itself. The SNMP panel below is a separate example of an observation block: it demonstrates units, sources, and context, but its readings are illustrative.
Use notation when it clarifies the explanation: a linear scan takes \(O(n)\), while repeated halving takes \(O(\log n)\). Define unfamiliar symbols before relying on them.

Keep a short status beside its claim: :badge[Illustrative]{neutral} marks an example, :badge[Supported]{positive} names an established capability, :badge[Needs evidence]{warning} flags a gap, and :badge[Blocked]{danger} identifies a blocker. These labels are static annotations, not controls or live readings.

blocks.title: Explain an equation, not just its symbols
blocks.description: The arithmetic mean mu is the sum of the n supplied values, divided by n. Here n must be greater than zero.
blocks.caption_md: This is a **definition**, not a measured result. The explanation names both the operation and its constraint.

blocks.title: Compare supplied quantities
blocks.context: Illustrative example only: a synthetic batch of 100 requests, not observed traffic.
blocks.caption: Each bar starts at zero. Values are counts, not percentages of the longest bar.

blocks.title: Show the interface being explained
blocks.alt: Illustrative teardown page titled A clear reading path, with a tip to lead with the answer and keep evidence beside its claim.
blocks.caption_md: A screenshot of a **synthetic example**, embedded from a local PNG. The HTML needs no companion files.

blocks.title: SNMP snapshot, illustrative readings
blocks.caption_md: **Illustrative readings, not live data.** For real observations, record the host and collection time. Source identifiers let the reader trace each value; the renderer never polls a server.

blocks.title: “Unsupported” is a conclusion, not a default.
blocks.body_md: If you have not checked whether a capability exists, label it **unknown**. A confident-looking card should not turn missing evidence into a negative finding.

items.question: What does the reader need to decide?
items.context_md: Choose the opening conclusion and the supporting blocks around that decision. A block inventory is not an argument.

items.question: Which claims still need evidence?
items.context_md:
Keep **unknown** separate from **unsupported**. To close a gap:

- Name the missing source and why it matters.
- Ask the owner or inspect the relevant contract.

terms.definition: The allowed structure of a document: its fields, values, and block shapes.
The program that turns a valid content document into a reading surface.
An observation or source that supports a particular claim. A polished layout is not evidence.
